newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa plans new employment strategy - minister.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa plans new employment strategy - minister.

text.p: South Africa is planning a strategy to boost employment through its macro- and microeconomic policies, Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said on Thursday.

Mboweni, who is also head of policy in President Nelson Mandela's ruling African National Congress, told parliament that the labour department could not on its own tackle unemployment, which he estimated at 33 percent.

"Job creation flows from the investment structure and macroeconomic policies, which define demand for labour. More jobs also flow out of factors that influence the cost and productivity of workers," he said.
Government departments were working together on an employment strategy to be submitted to the cabinet soon and to parliament in mid-May, he said.

"Critical areas of this strategy include enhanced support for labour-intensive industries and small and micro enterprise; reducing the cost of living; and increasing investment in human capital and local economic development programmes," he said.
Mboweni reaffirmed his intention to promote labour market flexibility, as required by the macroeconomic strategy for growth, employment and redistribution published last June.
That strategy seeks an average of 400,000 jobs created every year by the end of the century.
Mboweni warned industry not to confuse enhanced labour market flexibility with reduced job security.
"Unemployment does not arise from the nature of the labour market alone, but from the overall structure of the economy and its performance."
"We will support policies and activities which encourage greater and more productive use of labour without undermining worker security and basic employment conditions," he said.
